entities.name: Keranos
entities.description: God of storms and insight on Theros, embodying lightning and sudden inspiration; impatient, indifferent to morality.

entities.name: Theros
entities.description: Plane where Keranos is a god.

entities.name: Queen Cymede
entities.description: Queen of Akros and Keranos's most prominent devotee, taken from Akros before the Great Revel.

entities.name: Akros
entities.description: City-state of Queen Cymede, where Keranos rites were held.

entities.name: Thassa
entities.description: God with whom Keranos shares mutual respect and philosophical debates.

entities.name: Purphoros
entities.description: God with whom Keranos has a volatile but productive relationship.

entities.name: Epiphany
entities.description: Keranos's mighty javelin, born of his collaboration with Purphoros.

entities.name: Silence of the Gods
entities.description: The event that prevented the gods of Theros from contacting mortals.

entities.name: Rhordon
entities.description: Invading minotaur army destroyed by a steam elemental.

entities.name: Deyda River
entities.description: River Cymede raised into a steam elemental.

entities.name: Meletis
entities.description: City holding the Lightning Festival for Keranos.

entities.name: Great Revel
entities.description: Event before which Keranos took Cymede from Akros.

events.summary: Keranos circumvents the Silence of the Gods by sending prophetic visions to Queen Cymede, helping her destroy the minotaur army of Rhordon with a steam elemental.
events.quote: he circumvented the Silence by sending prophetic visions to Queen Cymede

events.summary: As a reward for her faith, Keranos takes Cymede from Akros shortly before the Great Revel.
events.quote: Keranos took her from Akros shortly before the Great Revel

relations.quote: Queen Cymede of Akros was his most prominent devotee
he shares a mutual respect with Thassa

relations.note: volatile but productive; made Epiphany together
relations.quote: Their collaboration gave rise to Epiphany, Keranos’s mighty javelin.
